filename: Deep Generative Data Assimilation in Multimodal Setting.pdf
title: Deep Generative Data Assimilation in Multimodal Setting
testbed_rationale: The paper presents a methodology and proof-of-concept evaluation for multimodal data assimilation via score-based latent diffusion; it does not produce a benchmark testbed or dataset designed for parameterization learning.
pain_points: Conventional DA methods rely on restrictive linear and Gaussian assumptions and computationally prohibitive tangent linear/adjoint formulations.
Formulating and calibrating the observation operator H to map state space to observation space is prone to error accumulation and bias in multimodal settings.
Real-world observations exhibit severe multimodality, differing spatiotemporal resolutions, noise, and spatial/temporal sparsity.
Diffusion posterior sampling suffers from numerical instabilities during reverse denoising when approximating likelihood scores with division by small state variances.
extraction_notes: Training window used years 2000-2015, validation 2016-2021, and test on 2022. Ground truth states were represented by ERA5 vertical temperature profiles.
